<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real.** `scripts/smoke.sh:165-166,179` still hard-codes the key ids and secrets with no compile-time link to the Go constants.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Merged into TKT-117 — do not claim

This ticket's scope now lives in **TKT-117** (Journal keyring operability: startup key fingerprint + link the smoke key literals to their Go constants), which carries it verbatim under an *Absorbed TKT-118* section. Moved out of Ready so it cannot be picked up in parallel. Nothing was dropped — reopen this only if the merge is reversed at plan time.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Closed as merged into TKT-117

Board validation 2026-08-08. This ticket's own summary has said `[MERGED into TKT-117]` since it was
folded in, but it was never transitioned — so it kept occupying Backlog and inflating the count of
outstanding work. **TKT-117 is Done**, verified before closing this.

No stage durations: the work was carried out under TKT-117 and its metrics belong there. This closure
is bookkeeping, not delivery.

**retro:** merging ticket B into ticket A needs to *close* B, not just retitle it. Six tickets
carried a `[MERGED into …]` marker in Backlog; the marker was written for a human reader and no
step ever acted on it. A summary prefix is not a state transition.

summary: [MERGED into TKT-117] Link the smoke journal key literals to their Go constants (TKT-56/S4 ai-review)
description:
Incidental finding from TKT-56 Slice 4's adversarial review (fable-5).

scripts/smoke.sh hard-codes the v1/v2 journal key ids and secrets (and the base64 of the v1 secret) for the packaged-binary verify-journal checks; journal_smoke_test.go declares the same values as smokeKIDv1/smokeKIDv2/smokeKeyv1/smokeKeyv2. There is no compile-time link between them.

Cosmetic today: drift fails LOUDLY (the positive packaged check fails, or the fixture guard trips), so this is maintainability, not correctness — which is exactly why it was not fixed inside the TKT-56 diff. Options: have the Go test emit the values to a file smoke.sh sources, or a tiny subcommand that prints them.
